records.note: Messengers acknowledge shared humanity but claim divine favor and authority only by God's permission; investigate distinct prophetic commissioning passages without assuming a direct parallel.
Messengers place trust in God while enduring harm. General persecution and fidelity motif; no exact prior textual relationship established.

Opponents threaten expulsion unless messengers return to the opponents' religion; God promises destruction of wrongdoers. Daniel 3:4-6 offers a different coercive worship scenario, not exile and not the same named actors.

candidates.similarity: Powerful opponents demand religious conformity under threat.
candidates.difference: Daniel concerns a Babylonian king's decree to worship a statue on pain of furnace execution; Q14:13 speaks collectively of opponents threatening messengers with expulsion or return to their religion, followed by divine judgment.
candidates.source_composition_note: Daniel's narrative setting is Babylonian; composition and surviving manuscript dates must be distinguished before publication.
candidates.pending: Check Aramaic Daniel 3 text in critical edition, Greek textual traditions, manuscript dating, and whether the comparison is distinctive enough to retain.

records.note: Promise to settle messengers in land after opponents; investigate covenantal land succession and prophetic victory traditions, but no passage-specific source checked.
Seeking judgment/victory and downfall of obstinate tyrants is general judgment language; no precise pre-Islamic textual parallel established in bounded pass; negative finding not exhaustive.

historical_dossier.topic: Prophetic authority, coercion and threatened expulsion in Q14:11-15
historical_dossier.comparison: Q14:13 and Daniel 3 share a general coercion motif but differ in actors, threatened sanctions, worship demands and outcome. No textual dependence established.
